stories.headline: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from crypto exchange Binance in massive cyber heist
stories.body:
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from cryptocurrency exchange Binance in a record cyber heist [c1]. The company froze around half of the stolen funds after the attack occurred [c1]. Binance secured $3 billion of its stolen digital assets [c2]. Unidentified hackers held the remaining funds [c2].

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM reported that an attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets [c14]. The funds were moved across ten blockchains, mostly within 20 minutes [c14]. NyxLab CEO Kok Tin Gan said the attack appeared to involve one signature [c17]. That signature granted a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet [c17].

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said hackers used a self-destruct mechanism [c6]. The mechanism destroyed tooling and traces as they went [c6]. Analytics firms linked the Binance hack to a North Korean hacking unit [c3]. Experts including TRM Labs attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean unit also called Lazarus Group [c10]. Chainalysis co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin said on X that the group likely did the attack [c15].

Cryptocurrency theft generates an estimated half of North Korea's foreign currency income [c12]. A UN panel of experts reported in spring 2024 that it was reviewing 58 suspected North Korean cyber-attacks [c11]. Those attacks targeted cryptocurrency companies between 2017 and 2023, and they were worth $3 billion [c11]. In February 2016, North Korean hackers tried to move $951 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York [c13]. They ultimately stole $81 million in that attack [c13].

The Binance heist eclipsed a $1.5 billion hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025 [c4]. Binance set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets [c7]. The US Secret Service said it was working around the clock to identify, freeze, trace, and recover stolen funds [c5]. The price of Bitcoin fell 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York after news of the hack [c8].

Binance was founded in China in 2017 [c9]. It has an estimated total of over 300 million registered users worldwide [c9]. Former Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform [c16]. US President Donald Trump pardoned Zhao in 2025 [c16].

vocab.meaning: a digital tool used to store cryptocurrency access keys
a digital code used to authorize a cryptographic transaction

stories.headline: Israeli general election ends in deadlock as Benjamin Netanyahu falls short of majority
stories.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed to win a parliamentary majority in the national election [c28]. His Likud party won 27 seats, remaining the largest party in the Knesset [c28]. But his right-wing coalition won 53 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority [c28]. A rival bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats [c22].

Netanyahu accused Palestinian Israeli parties of stealing the election and receiving money from Qatar [c18]. Israel's Electoral Commission found no evidence of fraud regarding Palestinian Israeli parties [c19]. Qatar also denied involvement [c19]. Acting Central Elections Committee Director General Dean Livne said there was no basis for allegations of systematic violations [c23]. Israeli security agency Shin Bet investigated whether Arab-led parties received illegal foreign funding from Qatar and Turkey [c20].

Arab Israelis make up about one-fifth of Israel's population [c24]. The Arab party lists The Joint List and Ra'am won a record 19 seats following high turnout [c21]. US President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu before the election [c30]. In Israel, a candidate given a mandate to form a government has 28 days to get support from 61 lawmakers, with a possible 14-day extension [c29].

vocab.meaning: a temporary alliance of political parties joining together
a number of seats greater than half of the total count

stories.headline: Civilians leave Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare localized ceasefire
stories.body:
Hundreds of residents left the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky during a four-hour ceasefire on Friday [c31]. US First Lady Melania Trump brokered the localized humanitarian ceasefire in the city [c32]. The population of Oleshky fell from a pre-war total of 24,000 to about 2,000 [c35].

Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia said evacuated residents traveled to Anapa in Russia [c33]. From there, they will fly to Belarus and travel by bus to Ukraine [c33]. Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said 25 buses and nine ambulances helped with evacuations [c34]. The ceasefire allowed workers to de-mine roads leading out of Oleshky [c37].

Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said this was the first long frontline ceasefire maintained since 2022 [c40]. The Kremlin described the Oleshky ceasefire as a special case that is hard to apply to broader peace talks [c38]. Russian forces captured Oleshky in February 2022 [c39]. The city suffered severe flooding after the Kakhovka dam was destroyed in June 2023 [c39]. In another attack, a Russian drone strike on a train station in Dnipro killed at least 13 people on Thursday [c36].

vocab.meaning: a temporary stop in military conflict agreed between sides
an official appointed to investigate public complaints

stories.headline: Polish police enter Constitutional Tribunal as head judge faces suspension
stories.body:
Polish police entered the Constitutional Tribunal building in Warsaw after demonstrators threw objects at officers [c41]. Demonstrators gathered outside the court during the protest [c41]. Supporters of the opposition Law and Justice party chanted that Tusk was a traitor and prayed outside [c50].

Authorities suspended Constitutional Tribunal head Bogdan Swieczkowski [c42]. He had used his power to block judges elected by the parliamentary majority from working [c42]. Justice Minister Waldemar Zurek requested that legal immunity be removed for Swieczkowski and his deputy so they could face criminal charges [c43]. Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska was put in charge of the court after the suspension [c46].

The Constitutional Court stated on social media that the actions against its top judges were a coup [c47]. It insisted that the judges remain legally appointed [c47]. Polish President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around while flying to Senegal [c45]. He said the president must be in Poland during the court crisis [c45]. Nawrocki has refused to swear in five court judges elected by parliament since March [c48]. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said restoring the rule of law after years of Law and Justice party lawlessness is a difficult process [c44].

vocab.meaning: a court of justice or official legal body

stories.headline: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta closes after state pressure
stories.body:
Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced its closure after being evicted from its central Moscow office [c51][c60]. Landlords told staff they must vacate the newsroom of 30 years by November 9 [c51][c60]. Authorities also blocked the newspaper from receiving reader donations [c51].

Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov wrote on the website that the newspaper was in a kill zone after nearly five years of working while surrounded by security services [c56]. Police questioned Sokolov and searched his home earlier in 2026 [c55]. That search was connected to investigative journalist Oleg Roldugin, who was arrested and charged with unlawful access to computerized information [c54].

Six Novaya Gazeta journalists have been killed over the years, including Anna Politkovskaya, who was shot dead in October 2006 [c53]. Co-founder Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 [c52]. Russian authorities labeled him a foreign agent in 2023 [c52]. Someone doused Muratov with red paint on a train in April 2022, which damaged his eyesight [c58]. After Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the newspaper printed blank white spaces to show censored text [c57]. Exiled journalists set up Novaya Gazeta Europe [c59].

vocab.meaning: legally forced to leave a rented property
officially removed or suppressed by authorities

stories.headline: Six people die after helicopter carrying pilgrims crashes near Joshimath in Uttarakhand
stories.body:
Six people died after a helicopter carrying pilgrims crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand on Friday [c61][c73]. The aircraft was operated by Trans Bharat [c69]. It took off from the pilgrimage site of Badrinath at 1:14 pm on Friday carrying six people before going missing [c74][c78]. It crashed in the Hathi Parvat area of Chamoli district while flying to Sahastradhara helipad in Dehradun [c77].

Pilot Captain Himanshu died in the crash alongside five passengers from Bengaluru [c79][c80]. The passengers were identified as Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K, and HS Natraja [c79]. Weather officials had issued an orange alert for the region, warning of thunderstorms, hail, and strong winds [c75].

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the helicopter came down near a village close to Joshimath [c76]. The Uttarakhand government grounded the entire Trans Bharat fleet after the accident [c70]. The civil aviation ministry recorded six helicopter accidents during the Char Dham Yatra between 2021 and June 2025 [c65]. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau recorded eight accidents and one serious incident in the Char Dham sector between 2015 and 2025 [c63].

vocab.meaning: a person who travels to a sacred place for religious reasons
a defined geographical area or zone

stories.headline: ISRO successfully launches NVS-03 navigation satellite aboard GSLV-F18 rocket
stories.body:
The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Friday [c81]. A GSLV-F18 rocket carried the satellite into space from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota [c81]. Liftoff occurred at 11:51 pm Indian Standard Time on October 30, 2026, from the Second Launch Pad [c92]. The rocket measured 51.7 metres tall [c92].

The GSLV-F18 rocket placed the 2,250 kg NVS-03 satellite into geosynchronous transfer orbit 18 minutes after liftoff [c82]. ISRO accomplished the GSLV-F18 mission with a turnaround time of 56 days after the earlier GSLV-F17 mission [c85].

ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan stated that the mission restored the NavIC constellation to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites [c83]. NavIC was originally designed with a constellation of seven satellites placed in geostationary and geosynchronous orbits [c88]. But the last functioning atomic clock aboard the IRNSS-1F satellite stopped working on March 13, 2026 [c84]. That left only three operational satellites in the NavIC system [c84].

India's armed forces rely on foreign navigation systems like US GPS and Russian GLONASS when NavIC has fewer than four operational satellites [c87]. The success of NVS-03 restores that minimum requirement [c83]. The replacement satellite NVS-02 failed to reach its intended orbit on January 29, 2025, because of a pyro valve signal loss in its engine [c89]. For this launch, ISRO kept specific valves open before liftoff to prevent the same technical problem from happening again [c93].

The NVS-03 satellite carries an indigenously manufactured atomic clock alongside imported atomic clocks [c86]. The satellite transmits signals in the L1, L5, and S bands [c90]. These signals make NavIC compatible with modern civilian smartphone chipsets [c90]. In June 2025, the Indian government announced plans to replace US GPS with five atomic clocks located across India to maintain Indian Standard Time [c91].

vocab.meaning: a group of satellites working together in space
produced or manufactured locally in a country

stories.headline: Oil tankers carrying Indian seafarers targeted in Strait of Hormuz attacks
stories.body:
Explosive devices damaged an oil tanker carrying Indian seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday [c95][c102]. The Panama-flagged oil tanker MT Louise 1 was carrying 27 Indian seafarers when it was targeted with limpet mines [c102]. The attack damaged the ship's engine room and temporarily disabled the vessel before crew members controlled an onboard fire [c104].

On October 29, the Liberia-flagged MT Arzanah was hit in a projectile attack in the Strait of Hormuz while carrying two Indian nationals [c105]. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that all 29 Indian seafarers across both ships were safe [c103]. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar raised concerns about attacks on civilian shipping during the G20 foreign ministers' meeting on Friday [c101].

The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported that a small boat attached explosive devices to a tanker on Friday [c95]. Limpet mines attach to a ship's hull using magnets to damage machinery [c106]. Meanwhile, the Omani Maritime Security Centre evacuated 25 crew members from the burning Panamanian-flagged oil tanker RITI on Friday [c98]. December Brent crude futures rose $2.76, or 2.4 percent, to settle at $117.64 a barrel on Friday [c94].

vocab.meaning: an explosive charge attached to a ship's hull using magnets
an object fired or thrown as a weapon
